title: Lift compatible etale coordinates through cotangent-fibre isomorphisms
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X,M_1,M_2$ finite-type $k$-schemes with $M_1,M_2$ smooth, $i_a:X\hookrightarrow M_a$ closed immersions, and $x\in X$. Put $L=\kappa(x)$ and suppose both canonical maps
$$\Omega_{M_a/k,i_a(x)}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{M_a,i_a(x)}}L\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}L$$
are isomorphisms. There is an integer $d=\dim_L(\Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes L)$ and, after restricting $X$ and the $M_a$ to affine neighbourhoods of the marked points, etale $k$-maps $e_a:M_a\to\mathbf A^d_k$ such that $e_1i_1=e_2i_2$ as morphisms on the restricted $X$. More precisely, any supplied etale coordinate chart $e_2$ to $\mathbf A^d_k$ near $i_2(x)$ can be used: its coordinate functions restrict to $X$ and admit lifts $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ on an affine neighbourhood in $M_1$; their differential classes form an $L$-basis of the ambient differential fibre, and the map $e_1=(g_j)$ is etale after further restriction. Thus the agreement is on the scheme $X$, including nilpotents, and not only on its residue field. The scheme notions, differential fibres and affine space are those of [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-sbc-affine-space].

source.place: Agent compatible-coordinate consequence of Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space, and Tag 02GU, lemma-etale-at-point; algebra.tex Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, for the differential basis of an etale chart. Retains old item Step 4.

proof.text: If no chart is supplied, apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] to $M_2\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $i_2(x)$, obtaining an affine neighbourhood $V_2$ and an etale chart $e_2:V_2\to\mathbf A^n_k$. Otherwise take an affine neighbourhood $V_2$ of $i_2(x)$ inside the domain of the supplied chart and let $e_2$ be its restriction to $V_2$, which is etale by open-immersion etaleness and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. In both cases $V_2$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme: it is affine, hence quasi-compact, and covered by principal opens of the finitely generated affine charts of $M_2$. Write $t_j=e_2^*T_j$. By [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-derivations-jacobian], the $dt_j$ are a basis of $\Omega_{\Gamma(V_2)/k}$. The affine description of the differential sheaf identifies its stalk with the localization of this free module, so its fibre at $i_2(x)$ has the basis $dt_j\otimes1$. A closed immersion identifies the residue fields at corresponding points (localize $B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$ and take residue fields). Thus this is an $L$-basis. The assumed second fibre isomorphism makes its images a basis of $\Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes L$, proving $n=d$. This also shows that any supplied chart has the required number of coordinates.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; algebra.tex Tags 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega, and 00RX, lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring; affine free-module fibre calculation.

proof.text: Put $X_2=i_2^{-1}(V_2)$. Since $i_1$ is a closed immersion, $i_1(X\setminus X_2)$ is closed in $M_1$ and misses $i_1(x)$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U_1$ of $i_1(x)$ in its complement. Then $X_1=i_1^{-1}(U_1)$ is contained in $X_2$ and is affine: by [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $X_1=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$. Restrict each $t_j$ to $X_1$ and choose $g_j\in B$ mapping to this section under $B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$. Define $h:U_1\to\mathbf A^d_k$ by $T_j\mapsto g_j$. Its restriction to $X_1$ is $e_2i_2|_{X_1}$, since their ring maps have identical values on constants and every polynomial variable. This equality takes place in $B/I$, without reducing it.

source.place: Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion, affine quotient characterization; elementary polynomial universal property.

proof.text: Let $\alpha_a:\Omega_{M_a/k,i_a(x)}\otimes L\to\Omega_{X/k,x}\otimes L$ be the stipulated isomorphisms. The universal derivation gives the canonical map on differentials under a ring map, by $db\mapsto d\bar b$; these maps agree on restrictions and germs. Hence $\alpha_1(dg_j\otimes1)=d(g_j|_{X_1})\otimes1=d(t_j|_{X_1})\otimes1=\alpha_2(dt_j\otimes1)$. The right-hand family is a basis by Step 1. Applying the inverse of $\alpha_1$ proves that the $dg_j\otimes1$ are an $L$-basis of the first ambient differential fibre. Restriction to $U_1$ has not changed this stalk or residue field.

source.place: Section on differentials, canonical functorial map (equation-functorial-omega); universal derivation and elementary transport of a basis through an isomorphism.

proof.text: The affine open $U_1$ is smooth and finite type over $k$: smoothness is local on the source, and it is affine, hence quasi-compact, and covered by principal opens of the finitely generated affine charts of $M_1$, so it is of finite type over $k$. Apply [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] to the specified functions $g_j$ and their basis from Step 3. There is an open neighbourhood $E\subset U_1$ of $i_1(x)$ on which $h$ is etale. Choose a principal neighbourhood $U'_1=D(b)\subset E$ in the affine $U_1$. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], and the restricted map remains etale by open-immersion etaleness and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Set $X'_1=i_1^{-1}(U'_1)$; it is an affine open of $X$, contained in $X_2$.

source.place: Tag 02GU, lemma-etale-at-point (8), chosen-coordinate consequence; schemes.tex Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; open restrictions of etale maps.

proof.text: Here is the common affine restriction, without an affineness assumption on intersections. For the affine opens $X'_1,X_2$ containing $x$, choose a principal open $D_{X_2}(f)$ containing $x$ and contained in $X'_1$; then choose a principal $D_{X'_1}(g)$ containing $x$ and contained in $D_{X_2}(f)$. Write $g|_{D_{X_2}(f)}=a/f^N$ in $\Gamma(X_2)_f$. Then $W=D_{X'_1}(g)=D_{X_2}(f)\cap D_{X_2}(a)=D_{X_2}(fa)$, since the first principal open was chosen inside $D_{X_2}(f)$. Thus $W$ is principal in both. Lift its defining functions $g$ and $fa$ through the respective quotient maps $\Gamma(U'_1)\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma(X'_1)$ and $\Gamma(V_2)\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma(X_2)$. Their principal opens $U''_1\subset U'_1$ and $V'_2\subset V_2$ are affine neighbourhoods whose inverse images under $i_1,i_2$ are exactly the open subscheme $W$, including its structure sheaf. The last assertion follows by localizing the quotient: $(B/I)_{\bar c}=B_c/IB_c$.

source.place: Tag 01IW, lemma-standard-open-two-affines, explicit two-principal-open proof; Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine; quotient localization calculation.

proof.text: Replace $X$ by $W$, $M_1$ by $U''_1$ and $M_2$ by $V'_2$. The restricted immersions are closed, by the quotient-localization description in Step 5. Define $e_1=h|_{U''_1}$ and keep the restriction of the original $e_2$ on $V'_2$. Both are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Step 2 already gave their agreement on $X_1$, so it gives $e_1i_1=e_2i_2$ on $W$. The restricted $g_j$ are the required lifts, and their differential classes are still the basis of Step 3. All neighbourhoods contain the marked points. For $d=0$ the list is empty and the same differential criterion applies; no smoothness, reducedness or separability assumption on $X$ has been used.

source.place: Tags 02GK and 02GN, open immersions are etale and composition of etale morphisms; assembly of the coordinate construction.

proof.text: Lean assembly of the compatible-chart clause from the supplied-chart clause (the latter retains the proof plan in Steps 1--6): choose an affine neighbourhood of i_2(x) and apply sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form to the smooth map q_2. Compose the resulting chart with AffineSpace.map of the target-open inclusion. This map is etale by base change of the open inclusion; AffineSpace.map_over and resLE_comp_ι identify its projection with V_2.ι ≫ q_2. Apply the existing exists_lift_of_etale_coordinates_of_cotangent_isomorphisms to this supplied chart. Retain its n=d, affine opens, membership and inverse-image equalities, and define e_1=homOfVector(g), e_2'=homOfLE(hV_2) ≫ e_2. Open-immersion composition proves etaleness of the second restriction; homOfVector_over proves the first projection equation, and homOfLE_ι proves the second. Associativity turns the supplied-chart equality into the required agreement on W. No coordinate basis or residue-field transport is reproved in this assembly.
